dryRunSoak._comment: Deploy requires a separate, proven transition after a FULL DryRun soak: hours is floored at 24; every gap between successful DryRun runs must be <= maxGapMinutes (task runs every 10 minutes).

writeScan._comment: Static detection of Ameen write capability in changed files (case-insensitive regexes, shared by the release workflow and the gate). A defence in depth only: every script uses a SQL login that can write, so the real control is a read-only login for readers (separate owner decision).

mainWorktree._comment: Dedicated main checkout ONLY for tasks that must run on main (Codex P1 #5). Never a path to update operational Windows scripts: the gate never touches it and run-repo-task.ps1 refuses scripts outside repoPath. It must be a separate worktree/clone on main with the official remote before the operational repo is switched to windows-production.

trust._comment: Future installation design only (nothing installed, no account created). The gate runs under a dedicated local identity that runs no code from tobacco-web or any other repository. SYSTEM, OZKSync, LOQ and Administrators are rejected: repository code already runs as SYSTEM (OZK-AmeenAutoPrint -> tools/ameen-autoprint/run-watcher.bat via install-service.bat), as LOQ (a member of Administrators) and as OZKSync, and SYSTEM/Administrators can override ACLs. The trust files are writable only by the dedicated identity; repository workload identities get read-only access. A local administrator can still technically take ownership: this separates automation trust domains so repository code cannot change the gate's trust state; it is not a defence against a malicious human administrator.
trust._trustAnchorComment: Highest ancestor of gateDir whose ACL is analysed for container-replacement capability (delete/rename child, take control). Levels between the immediate parent and the anchor need not be exclusive to the gate; SYSTEM, Administrators, TrustedInstaller and local Administrators members are OS-administrative trust there, because any automated repository workload running as one of them already blocks Initialize. The anchor itself is OS-managed; its own replaceability depends on its parent (C:\), where only OS-administrative principals hold delete rights by default.
